summary: Preserved candidate PR 2946's pre-stream MTP shard selection and corrected its mixed-layout safety gap: an index containing a supported requested-layer key plus an unrecognized MTP/NextN namespace now falls back to the complete prepared shard list.

tests.what_was_measured: At exact candidate e9952a5825d098de1c068d061062fe2522981d27, the RunAI iterator received only draft-1.safetensors instead of the complete five-file prepared list. Raw output: reports/j-6f4bf626a186/failing-before.txt

17 focused loader tests and 6 subtests passed, covering supported layout selection, shared parameters, object-storage metadata paths, malformed/missing/incomplete/unknown indexes, auto-added MTP files, and the mixed-layout counterexample. Raw output: reports/j-6f4bf626a186/passing-after.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The corrected behavior is deterministic JSON key classification and filename-list selection before tensor streaming; no model weights or tensor computation are involved, so GPU execution would not validate this defect.

remaining_limitations: No live object-storage credentials or production MTP checkpoint were available; provider header-read counts, distributed loading, and end-to-end model semantics remain unverified.

Unknown draft layouts are conservatively detected by MTP or NextN namespace components. Layouts with no draft-signaling namespace remain indistinguishable from ordinary target-model keys and therefore cannot be classified without architecture-specific evidence.
